2. The petitioner bank filed the money 'Execution No.8/98 for satisfaction of the decree dated 27.5.98 passed in Artha Rin Case No.5/97 by the Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Kurigram. The decree was for Tk. 13,79,745.27 paisa. The execution case was disposed of holding that the decree passed in the suit has been satisfied vide order dated 8.1.2004 passed in Money Execution Case No.8/98 by the Artha Rin Adalat No.1 Kurigram, on an application filed by the judgment-debtor under Section-47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. 

 3. Being aggrieved the petitioner bank preferred Civil Revision Case No.6/04 before the District Judge, Kurigram, along with tin application under Section.-5 of Limitation for condonation of delay of 54 days and the learned District judge rejected the revision case, holding that revision case does not lie, whereupon the petitioner bank preferred Artha Rin AppealNo.1/04 against the said order dated 8.1.04 passed in the execution case. The learned District Judge considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the submission of the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner bank dismissed the appeal on the ground of limitation holding, amongst others, that as per Section 41 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, an appeal has to be filed within 30 clays and the appeal has been filed beyond the prescribed 30 (thirty) days and thus barred by limitation. 

 4. Being aggrieved the petitioner bank filed the instant revisional case and obtained the Rule. 

 6. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submitted that there was delay in preferring the appeal because of misconception of the law on the part of the learned advocate for which initially a revision case was preferred against the impugned order passed in the execution case and subsequently the appeal has been filed, and as such the delay in preferring the appeal was not intentional and there was no fault on the part of the petitioner bank, Because of misunderstanding of the law on the part of the concern learned advocate the petitioner bank should not suffer loss. The learned Advocate however could not show us any provision of law for condoning any delay in respect of any proceedings or case under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. The learned Advocate also submitted that the impugned order passed by the Executing Court was without jurisdiction, inasmuch as the suit was filed in the. year 1997, whereas the benefit given under the provision of Section-47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 was effective' from 9th March, 2004 vide said Section 47 and as such the claim of the judgment debtor as to satisfaction of the decreetal amount was without any basis, inasmuch as the judgment debtor is not entitled to any relief under the Section-47 of the Artha Rin Ain, 2003 and thus the impugned order dated 8.1.04 passed by the Executing Court regarding satisfaction of the decree was illegal. The entertainment of the application for recording satisfaction of the decree by the Executing Court is without jurisdiction.
